title: Functional Benefits of Multisite Upper Limb Surgery in Children With Unilateral Cerebral Palsy (RETRO-CHIRc)
official: Retrospective Study of Functional Benefits of Individualized Multisite Neuro-Orthopedic Upper Limb Surgery in Children With Unilateral Cerebral Palsy
summary: This retrospective study evaluates the functional impact of individualized multisite neuro-orthopedic upper limb surgery in children with unilateral cerebral palsy (hemiplegic CP). Using a before-and-after design in which each patient serves as their own control, the study analyzes data collected in routine clinical care up to 3-5 years before and 1-2 years after surgery. The primary outcome is upper limb function as measured by the Modified Melbourne Assessment (MA2), which assesses range of motion and dexterity. Secondary outcomes include unimanual precision and fluidity (MA2), global manual dexterity (Box and Block Test), bimanual performance (Assisting Hand Assessment), and patient/parent satisfaction. Approximately 70 patients operated at the Centre Médico-Chirurgical de Réadaptation des Massues between January 2012 and June 2025 will be included. The study also aims to identify factors influencing surgical outcomes, such as age at surgery, associated cognitive or sensory impairments, and adherence to post-operative orthotic protocols.
criteria:
INCLUSION CRITERIA

* Minor patient (age \< 18 years at the time of the surgical project)
* Unilateral upper limb involvement due to Cerebral Palsy
* Having undergone neuro-orthopedic upper limb surgery
* Surgery performed by the surgeon who participated in the multidisciplinary surgical planning meeting (EMC)
* Surgery performed between January 1, 2012 and June 30, 2025
* Availability of at least one pre-operative assessment and one comparative post-operative assessment at more than 12 months after surgery
* Followed at the CMCR des Massues

NON-INCLUSION CRITERIA

* Refusal of medical data processing for research purposes
